claim_text: Rackspace told customers an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot on Nov 17
summary: BleepingComputer quotes Rackspace's customer notice: 'On 17 November 2026 (about 00:20–22:00 UTC), an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot.'
detail: The notice went to affected customers and was obtained by BleepingComputer. We could not read it ourselves, and Rackspace's public pages (release notes and status page) do not describe a breach. Held at Reported: one outlet relaying a private notice, with no Rackspace-hosted page we could cite.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer (Tier 2) quotes the notice; no official public page carries it.
notes: Upgrade to Confirmed if Rackspace publishes the notice or a statement on a page it hosts, or a second independent outlet confirms it.

claim_text: Rackspace says the unauthorized party could act as legitimate users in some customer organizations: create pods in Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes
summary: Per the notice as BleepingComputer reports it, attackers could read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, plus any Spot API or refresh tokens that user held. Rackspace learned of it Nov 18 after a customer report.
detail: 'Some customer organizations' is Rackspace's wording; it did not say how many. Rackspace says 'could have read', which is not a finding that any Secret was read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Only BleepingComputer's account of the private notice supports it.

claim_text: The Spot admin console was down for several days while Rackspace locked the platform down
summary: BleepingComputer says the breach caused an extended Spot admin console outage that stopped customers rotating credentials. It quotes a Spot co-developer on Reddit saying access was shut down deliberately to sanitize the environment.
detail: The Reddit post is quoted second-hand and we did not read it. On Nov 20 a Spot team member wrote on Spot's official GitHub Discussions forum that, because of the nature of the incident, the team was making several intrusive changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, causing the extended outage. That is a forum post, not a Rackspace statement. Rackspace's own status page and release notes do not describe the outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Outlet report, plus a Spot team member's forum post (Tier 4) describing the deliberate shutdown; neither is a Rackspace-hosted statement.

claim_text: Rackspace says Spot service was fully restored on Nov 21
summary: BleepingComputer says that after multiple delays Rackspace announced service was fully restored on Nov 21. Rackspace's status page, when we checked on Nov 21, showed no outage but a notice restricting new sign-ups.
detail: We could not find the restoration announcement on a Rackspace-hosted page. On the evening of Nov 20 (ET) a Spot team member wrote on Spot's GitHub Discussions forum that the team had missed its goal and expected full restoration by 9am Pacific on Nov 21. That is an estimate, not a restoration notice.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The outlet reports the announcement; the status page is consistent with service running but does not say it was restored; the forum post gives only an expected time.

claim_text: Rackspace says it revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed unauthorized pods, rotated keys and strengthened access controls, and told customers to rotate credentials
summary: Per BleepingComputer, customers were told to reissue Spot API tokens, replace refresh tokens, download fresh kubeconfig files, rotate cluster Secrets and review logs back to Nov 17.
detail: Rackspace also shared indicators of compromise with customers (an IP address, a range, and Kubernetes object name prefixes). We do not list them here.
label: Reported

claim_text: Rackspace's Spot release notes list a November 2026 fix that closed a network exposure on Spot worker nodes as part of security hardening
summary: The November 2026 entry says: 'We closed a network exposure on Spot worker nodes as part of ongoing security hardening.' The entry is undated and does not mention a breach or the Nov 17 access.
detail: This is on Rackspace's own page. Whether the fix relates to the Nov 17 access is not stated, so we do not link them.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Rackspace's own release notes (Tier 1) state it.

claim_text: Rackspace's Spot status page says new organization sign-ups are restricted until Nov 25, 17:00 UTC, after recent system maintenance operations
summary: The pinned notice says Rackspace is prioritizing capacity for existing customers and has paused new sign-ups; existing customers can keep bidding and running workloads. It does not mention a security incident.
detail: The notice was created on Nov 21 per the page. We do not know whether the maintenance is the lockdown described in the reports.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Rackspace's own status page (Tier 1) states it.

claim_text: Customer data was stolen or misused
summary: Rackspace has not said whether data was taken or any Secret was misused. BleepingComputer asked Rackspace and says it had no response when it published.
detail: The notice says Secrets could have been read, which is exposure, not confirmed theft or misuse.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source says data was taken or abused.

summary: No source gives a figure. The notice says 'some customer organizations'; BleepingComputer asked how many and got no reply.
label: Not established

summary: No source names an attacker, group or motive, and none reports a claim of responsibility or ransom demand.
detail: Rackspace shared technical indicators with customers; that is not an attribution.
label: Not established

claim_text: The root cause: how the credentials leaked and whose they were
summary: Rackspace says the credentials were 'leaked'. A Spot team member wrote on Spot's GitHub forum on Nov 20 that an observability system was breached using a compromised credential. Whose credential, and how it leaked, is not known.
detail: No incident report has been published. The forum post is a short explanation from a team member, not a published root cause. No closure without a published root cause.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The notice and a forum post (Tier 4) give only a short description of the cause, with no detail or official report.

claim_text: A Spot team member said on Spot's official GitHub Discussions forum that an observability system was breached using a compromised credential
summary: On Nov 20 a Spot team member wrote: 'an observability system was breached using a compromised credential. This was obviously a critical error on our part'. The post says the cause was also discussed on Reddit and in emails to customers.
detail: The forum is Rackspace Spot's own GitHub Discussions board, linked from its status page, but a forum post is not a Rackspace statement, and BleepingComputer describes a Spot co-developer at Platform9 (which co-developed Spot with Rackspace) making similar remarks on Reddit. It is a separate account from the customer notice, so it supports the notice, but it is not a basis for Confirmed. It does not say what the observability system is or whose credential it was.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The forum post (Tier 4) states the cause in the team member's own words.
notes: Upgrade only with a Rackspace-hosted statement or incident report.
